source.display_title: 05/08/2026 - Tony & Farooq Bey - Kettlebell Body Game Plan Session — Lost

setter.evidence: No setter named by either party. The prospect said he had been watching Trevor's videos for a while and booked from that.

prospect.name: Tony Moore
prospect.location: Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; commutes daily to New York
prospect.occupation: Amtrak engineering department — electrical work on the overhead catenary system. Currently on emergency standby working midnight to 8am and sitting all night. Also owns a business consulting company, largely run day to day by his cousin, and trades stocks.
prospect.family_status: No children; nieces and nephews; describes a large family that looks to him for advice and guidance
prospect.training_background: Kinesiology degree from Penn State, so has an exercise science background, and has done personal training in the past. Training history is barbells and dumbbells only, never kettlebells. By his own account has done nothing consistently for 10 to 15 years. Fasts once a year for 15 or 30 days. Gym attendance is impractical because of a daily Philadelphia to New York commute and night shifts.
prospect.medical: Type 2 diabetes and high cholesterol, both known for around three years. Describes the diabetes himself as 'pretty much reversible if your diet, exercise, and lifestyle changes.' Poor sleep pattern and no energy through the day. Wakes stiff and sore — 'I felt like an old man... like I've been fighting in my sleep' — with hip and joint discomfort on standing, which he attributes to being sedentary. Sedentary for 10 to 15 years. Undertakes 15 to 30 day fasts annually.

signals: Wants a specific former self back and names the timeframe: 'I need to feel like I felt 20 years ago' and 'mentally, I feel like I'm 25, so I need to bridge that gap'
Lost ground across a long hard season — night shifts, commuting and work meant 'I just kind of fell off pretty much. I haven't done anything consistently within the past 15 years'
Carries visible regret and named it without prompting: 'the muscle mass is still there, but the fat's piled on now' and 'I take pride, always took pride in the way I appear'
Describes withdrawal as a consequence — putting on a shirt, seeing his stomach, and not going to the event

Secondary read worth noting on review: skeptical_bargain_hunter. He holds a kinesiology degree, believes he can self-direct given structure, asked specifically about a PDF routine he had seen advertised, and bought the cheapest available product. His resistance was scope and value, never affordability.

goals.text: Shed around 30 pounds and maintain a weight of about 220
Regain flexibility and functional mobility before turning 50
Wake up energetic rather than stiff and exhausted
Be practically strong for everyday movement rather than just able to push weight
Train at home, since a daily Philadelphia to New York commute and night shifts make a gym impractical
Be consistent for the first time in 10 to 15 years
Have the energy to spend time with family, check on older relatives, and be present for nieces and nephews
Be a role model who motivates his whole family — 'look at him, he's 50'
Recover the confidence he associates with being in shape, which he says radiates to others
Have the energy to grow his consulting business and do more market research
Reverse the type 2 diabetes through diet, exercise and lifestyle change

pains.text: Type 2 diabetes and high cholesterol, known for around three years
Sedentary and inconsistent for 10 to 15 years despite an exercise science background
Around 30 pounds above his target weight
Wakes stiff and sore with hip and joint discomfort — 'I felt like an old man'
Poor sleep pattern working midnight to 8am, and no energy through the day
Procrastination named as the primary blocker for 10 to 15 years
No accountability circle — 'most people are not health oriented... it all depends on your circle'
Withdrawn socially because of how clothes fit — declines events and stays home
Lacks the energy to engage with his consulting business, leaving it to his cousin
Daily Philadelphia to New York commute plus night shifts make gym attendance impossible
Low mood and enthusiasm — declines invitations to see nieces and nephews after work

objections.raw_quote: that's a little that's a little pricey that i thought the program would be... for me to just get something structured to go in something that would be four thousand dollars that that wouldn't make sense to me just because i have i have a little bit of background so if i had to figure it out you know i would rather figure out myself
objections.rep_response: Argued that if he had the capability to do it alone he would have done so over the past 10 to 15 years. The prospect corrected him: 'not really the capability, it's just the motivation.'

objections.raw_quote: I don't really need that intensive. I was looking at something structured to do, you know, maybe, okay, this day do this, this day do that... I understand it's worth its value of gold, but I don't think I really need it, you know what I mean? I don't really need that much
objections.rep_response: Reframed price as commitment — 'if you actually invested a high amount into yourself, you're going to be more or less committed?' — then asked how he would pay if he were to do it.

objections.raw_quote: Give me something a little bit less... I saw something on his page. He was advertising the kettlebell routine in a PDF. What do you offer in that? You know what saying? And something like that, you know, structured workouts. $4,000, I don't need to spend that much money on it.
objections.rep_response: Conceded the coaching was not the right fit — 'maybe the one-on-one coaching isn't for you, and that's fine' — and screen-shared Primal University at $199 per month. Never answered the question about the PDF.

offer.payment_plan_terms: None offered. The rep asked how he would pay if he were to proceed and accepted 'it would go on a credit card' without structuring anything, correctly reading the objection as scope rather than capacity.
offer.guarantee_mentioned: For Primal University only: 'It's just 200 bucks, okay? You can cancel it at any time. It says 200 bucks a month, but it can be canceled at any time. So some people come in for a month, they get the structure, they get a plan... and then they leave.' Annual option also offered at $2,000 including access to Trevor's live classes, which the monthly does not include.

evidence: The coaching programme was declined on scope and value, not affordability, and repeatedly: 'I don't really need anything that intensive', 'I don't need to spend that much money for something', 'that wouldn't make sense to me'
The rep conceded rather than continued: 'So maybe the one-on-one coaching isn't for you, and that's fine, right?'

The prospect explicitly separated worth from fit — 'I'm definitely not saying it's not worth the money... I could figure out a better economic way of getting there' — and confirmed he would have paid by credit card if he had wanted it
No programme tier was purchased and no follow-up call was booked; the prospect floated only a vague 'maybe in three or five months' of his own accord
What was sold instead is Primal University at $199 per month, completed live on the recording with the rep confirming the payment: 'Payment successful. We emailed you a receipt'
Counter-evidence: pre-price alignment was as strong as it gets — 'I think 100% this is going to be very good' — so this was a product-fit loss rather than a conviction loss
outcome.cash_collection_basis: First month of Primal University, a $199 per month cancel-anytime Skool subscription. Ancillary product revenue, not a programme sale — must not be counted in coaching close rate or contract value. This is the second of only two payments in this batch witnessed completing on the recording.
outcome.next_step: None agreed. Prospect has Primal University access and said he might revisit the coaching in three to five months once he has made progress; the rep did not book anything.

notable.note: The clinical picture is the finding and it has two parts. The prospect disclosed type 2 diabetes and high cholesterol known for three years, is roughly 30 pounds above his target weight, has been sedentary for 10 to 15 years, sleeps badly on a midnight to 8am shift and reports hip and joint pain. To the rep's credit he asked the best health question in this batch — 'Is there anything else I need to be aware of? Any limitations in your body?' followed by 'How long have we been aware of this?' — and then did nothing with the answer: no question about medication, no question about who is managing it, and no question about clearance for loaded ballistic training. Worse, he then actively promoted fasting to a diagnosed type 2 diabetic who already undertakes 15 to 30 day fasts annually: 'We're big on fasting too, especially as you enter our 50s, man.' Nobody asked whether he takes glucose-lowering medication. Separately, this is the third call in three days where the rep said 'We don't run a subscription model here' and then sold a monthly subscription, and the fourth prospect in this batch to ask to buy less than the full bundle.

quality.notes: Heavy inversion throughout, including whole blocks of the rep's pillar delivery under the prospect's label and vice versa. The section from roughly 00:42:03 to 00:42:50 loses punctuation and capitalisation entirely and merges several turns, as does the passage from 00:58:58 to 01:00:00; both were untangled from content. Roles resolved from content. Current weight of 250 lb is derived, not stated — the prospect said he wants to 'shed about 30 pounds and maintain a weight of about 220'; height was never asked. Age is derived from 'I'll be 50 in a few months.' Surname recovered from the speaker label, since the file title names him only as 'Tony'. The recording ran through the payment, which is unusual for this rep and makes this one of only two fully witnessed transactions in the batch.
